items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] He’s a controversial figure. Some people think he was like the Kenny G of his day.

ctx.x: Yeah. And opportunities to play in places that I hadn’t had with some of the other acts. Like we got to play the Clifford Brown Jazz Fest in Delaware, the Newport Jazz Fest, more of the jazz-oriented festivals. The Blue Notes in Italy and New York. And it was a different thing. And it was the right thing for me at the right time. So I didn’t leave Mike’s band to exclusively go with Chuck but I had been there a long time and I knew if I wanted to grow I should go do this. And it was wonderful.
He’s a controversial figure. Some people think he was like the Kenny G of his day. But he wrote such great hooks. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Yeah. I think his greatest strength was exactly what you just touched on. The melodies and the music to me personally were deeper than the modern day smooth jazzers. And I just thought he had a wonderful sense of melody and harmony and of course he’s a wonderful flugelhornist himself and hey, he played with Art Blakey you know. And he and Gerry Niewood had a special thing. I mean growing up together and playing all those years that they had together. I was lucky enough to play most of the time Gerry was there,…
